newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian MinFins unaffected by postponed debt deal.
newsitem.headline: Russian MinFins unaffected by postponed debt deal.

text.p: Prices of Russian MinFin bonds firmed mainly on positive news about President Boris Yeltsin's health and ahead of the Eurobond issue, dealers said on Monday.
Delays in Russia's deal with London Club of bank creditors failed to affect late thin trading, they said.
(NOTE - Sunday November 10 was a trading day in Russia)
The Russian finance ministry said on Monday the closure of the deal rescheduling Russia's commercial bank debt is not likely to take place until the first quarter of 1997.

"The news came too late to move anything as London operators have already finished trading because of the U.S. (Veterans' Day) holiday. There are few Russian operators left as well," Sberbank dealer Pavel Sool said.
Dealers said foreign buying had been seen earlier in the most actively traded fourth and fifth tranches, with current resistance levels at 59.50 and 42.50 respectively.

The market was in bullish mood, given the satisfactory condition of Yeltsin, recovering from last week's heart surgery, and the forthcoming issue of Russia's Eurobonds whose road-show started on Monday in Tokyo, dealers said.
Hopes the problem of frozen bonds will be resolved soon was another positive factor, they said.
"In principle, everybody is looking upwards," an ICFI Moscow Partners dealer said.
